title: PokeFun AlphaZone — Complete Player Guide
content:
PokeFun AlphaZone — Complete Player Guide

Last updated: June 2026

Table of Contents

  1. What is AlphaZone?
  2. How to Join
  3. Game Modes
  4. Alpha Points & Economy
  5. Level System
  6. Leaderboards
  7. Alpha Pokemon & Tiers
  8. Raid Events
  9. Loot Chests
  10. Match Rewards
  11. AlphaZone Shop
  12. Commands
  13. Tips & Strategy

1. What is AlphaZone?

AlphaZone is a Cobblemon PvP Battlegrounds system with 4 game modes. Players fight using their Pokemon inside battle arenas, with alpha boss spawns, loot chests, raid events, entry fees, leveling, and ranked progression.

Available Arenas (7)

  • Blazing Wastes
  • Crimson Arena
  • Crystal Mines
  • Forbidden Jungle
  • Frozen Abyss
  • Sample Arena
  • Skyward Colosseum

Each arena has different modes, player limits, and configurations. Join randomly or pick a specific arena.

2. How to Join

  1. Use /warp alphazone to go to the AlphaZone lobby.
  2. Open the AlphaZone menu from the lobby NPC or use /alphazone menu.
  3. Choose Random Join or select a specific arena.
  4. Wait in the lobby until enough players join — match starts automatically.
  5. Use /alphazone leave to leave at any time.

3. Game Modes

Royale Alpha Royale

Players: 2–20 | Win: Last player standing

  • 3 lives per player, respawn timer
  • Shrinking border — zone damage outside safe area
  • Alpha spawns, loot chests, raid events
  • Match timer (configurable, ends when 1 remains or time runs out)

FFA Free For All

Players: 1+ | Win: No winner — infinite PvP loop

  • Instant respawn (3s), infinite lives
  • No border, no time limit — join/leave anytime
  • Alpha events + raids enabled
  • Kill tracking for leaderboards

Imposter Imposter Mode

Players: 3–10 | Win: Imposter eliminates all OR crew survives 3 min / completes 5 tasks

  • 1 random player = imposter (hidden identity)
  • Tasks auto-complete every 30 seconds
  • Fixed 180s (3 min) match
  • No alpha events, no border, no raids

Team Team Duels

Players: 2–6 | Win: First team to 25 kills

  • Challenge via /alphazone duel <player> 1/2/3
  • 1v1, 2v2, or 3v3 battles
  • No alpha spawns, no border, no raids
  • Pure team PvP

4. Alpha Points & Economy

AlphaZone uses its own currency: Alpha Points (impactor:alpha_points) — completely separate from Dungeon Points.

How to Earn Alpha Points

  • Player Kills — kill another player to earn points
  • Alpha Kills — killing alpha Pokemon in the arena
  • Raid Participation — kill raid alphas and bosses
  • Loot Chests — opening chests in the arena
  • Wins — winning a Royale match
  • Survival Time — staying alive in the match

Point Steal System

Point Steal: When you eliminate a player, you steal ALL their match-earned Alpha Points. The victim's points reset to 0. This creates high-risk, high-reward gameplay.

Point Steal works in: Royale (yes), FFA (yes), Imposter (yes), Team Duels (yes — team with most kills wins).

5. Level System

Earn XP from player kills, alpha kills, raid participation, wins, and survival time. Level up to unlock rank titles and rewards.

LevelXP RequiredReward

2200Iron rank

105000Mewtwo Lv.50
2015000Legend rank
5050000Mythic rank

Check your stats: /alphazone stats

6. Leaderboards

AlphaZone tracks: Wins, Kills, Deaths, KD Ratio, Alpha Kills, Win Streak, Highest Streak, Level, XP.

  • /alphazone top wins — Top 10 by wins
  • /alphazone top kills — Top 10 by kills
  • /alphazone top level — Top 10 by level/XP
  • /alphazone leaderboard — Default (wins)

7. Alpha Pokemon & Tiers

Alpha Pokemon spawn during FFA and Royale matches. They cannot be captured. Killing them grants Alpha Points, XP, and rewards.

TierLevelDamage xHealth xPoints Reward
Tier 1501.0x1.0x10
Tier 2601.5x2.0x20
Tier 3702.0x3.0x30
Elite853.0x5.0x50
Boss Tier1005.0x10.0x100

Expanded Species: All tiers now include 285+ additional species including:

  • Fakemon — All custom fakemon species from the Fakemon Crate (Alloette, Beryllius, Gorochu, Godzillante, and 165+ more)
  • Fusion-exclusive Pokemon — Acideon, Blazetoise, Charredbone, Eeveeon, Wyveon, Pyrochu, and more
  • Paradox Pokemon — Fluttermane, Great Tusk, Iron Valiant, Walking Wake, and all others
  • Ultra Beasts — All Ultra Beasts across appropriate tiers
  • Form variants — Rotom forms, Gourgeist sizes, Calyrex forms, and more

Alpha events occur every ~25–60 seconds (configurable per arena). Max 3–5 alphas can be alive at once.

8. Raid Events

Periodic raid events trigger automatically during FFA and Royale matches:

  • A random player becomes the raid target
  • Waves of alpha Pokemon spawn near the target player
  • A boss Pokemon spawns midway through the raid
  • All alive players get completion rewards when the raid ends

Raid Rewards

  • Per kill: Alpha Points + XP for each alpha/boss killed
  • Completion: Bonus Alpha Points for all surviving players

Example Raid (Crimson Arena)

WaveEnemiesDelay
15x Tier 1 alphas0s
25x Tier 2 alphas~10s
32x Tier 5 alphas~15s
41x Elite alpha~25s
BossDialga (Boss Tier)~25s

9. Loot Chests

Chests spawn at fixed positions in each arena. Opening them gives random items:

10. Match Rewards

At the end of each match, rewards are distributed based on your rank/performance:

  • Alpha Points deposited to your balance
  • XP toward level progression
  • Random Pokemon from a weighted species list (with anime themes, mega evolutions, shiny variants)
  • Items & commands
  • Alpha Points (1–2) as item drops in each rank tier (reduced for economy balance)

Weighted Pokemon System

Higher weight = higher chance. Example:

  • Dragonite (weight 10) — common
  • Tyranitar (weight 8) — common
  • Mewtwo Shiny (weight 1) — rare
  • Rayquaza Shiny (weight 1) — rare
  • Aerodactyl (Solo Leveling aspect, weight 1) — rare
  • Greninja (various anime aspects, weight 1 each) — rare
  • Galactic aspect — Arcanine, Charizard, Dragonite, Lapras, Pidgeot, Rayquaza, Snorlax, Tyranitar with Galactic skin
  • Ho-Oh now available as a reward Pokemon

⚠️ Updated Economy

  • Match Points: 1st place=10pts, 2nd=5pts, 3rd=3pts, participant=1pt, win bonus=5pts
  • Per kill: Tier 1=0pts, Tier 2=1pt, Tier 3=2pts, Tier 4=4pts, Tier 5=6pts, Elite=10pts, Boss=15pts
  • End reward points: 1-2 points (item drop, 10% chance)
  • Zero cooldown: All arenas now have 0 min cooldown — play unlimited matches!
  • Target grind: ~25-35 points per FFA match. Cheapest key (ItemCrate=500pts) in ~5-6 hours of play

11. AlphaZone Shop

Spend your Alpha Points at the shop. Access via /alphazone shop.

12. Commands

CommandDescription

/alphazone menuOpen the main AlphaZone menu

/alphazone denyDeny a duel invite
/alphazone team add <player>Add player to your team

13. Tips & Strategy

Tip: Point Steal is huge. If you see someone with many kills, eliminate them to steal ALL their points. High risk, high reward.
Tip: Open loot chests early. Chests give items AND Alpha Points. Loot up before engaging other players.
Tip: Watch for raid events. When a raid starts, alphas spawn near the raid target. You can earn bonus points by participating — but also beware of enemy players attacking during the chaos.
Tip: Royale border shrinks. Stay inside the safe zone. The border deals damage to players and Pokemon outside it.
Tip: Use /alphazone stats to track progress. Check your wins, kills, KD ratio, and level to see how you're improving.
Tip: Save Alpha Points for shiny/rare keys. Shiny variant keys cost more but give shiny Pokemon. The Legendary + Shiny Key (8,400 AP) is endgame.
🎉 Zero Cooldown! All arenas now have 0 min cooldown — play unlimited matches back-to-back! Grind Alpha Points as much as you want.
Tip: Imposter mode tasks. Tasks auto-complete every 30 seconds. Survive 2.5 min and you win as crewmate. Find the imposter before they find you.
Note: Alpha Points are separate from Dungeon Points. You cannot spend Alpha Points in the Dungeon shop or vice versa.

title: BattleTower — Epic PvE Challenge 2 Towers · 20 Floors Each · Singles + Doubles · Player Cap Lv.1-45
content:
BattleTower — Epic PvE Challenge 2 Towers · 20 Floors Each · Singles + Doubles · Player Cap Lv.1-45

🏰 What is BattleTower? Fight through 20 progressive floors of NPC trainers. Each floor win gives currency, battletower_tokens, Rare Candies, and crate keys! Two towers: Sky Tower (Dragon/Flying theme) and Abyss Tower (Ghost/Dark theme).

🎮 How to Play (Flow)

Step-by-Step

  1. Start: Use /warp battletower or click the BattleTower NPC in spawn
  2. Choose Tower: Select Sky Tower or Abyss Tower from the menu
  3. Party Up: Team size 2-6 players (recommended: 4). All players must be Lv.1-45
  4. Battle: Each floor has 1-3 NPC trainers with Lv.22-65 Pokémon. Beat them all to advance
  5. Rewards: Each floor win gives instant rewards — currency, tokens, candies, crate keys
  6. Floor 20 ⭐: Boss floor! Defeat the tower boss for premium rewards
  7. Complete: Clear all 20 floors to get completion bonus (10,000 currency + 2 Nether Stars)
  8. Cooldown: After completion, you must wait 24 hours before replaying the same tower
💡 Tip: Build a balanced team of 4. Early floors use Singles, late floors use Doubles. Pokémon types are different every floor!

⏱ Cooldown System

🕐 Each tower has a 24-hour cooldown after you complete it. You can run Sky Tower one day and Abyss Tower the next day — or wait 24h to replay the same tower. The cooldown is per player, per tower — not shared!

🎯 BattleTower Tokens Shop

🪙 What are BattleTower Tokens? Earned on every floor win (30-220 per floor). Use them in the BattleTower Token Shop to buy exclusive items — including crate keys, Rare Candies, Master Balls, and more! Check the shop via /battletoken shop.

💡 Pro Tips

  • Run both towers — each has its own 24h cooldown, so you can do Sky today, Abyss tomorrow
  • Party up! Minimum 2 players, but 4 is ideal. More players = easier clears
  • Floor 20 is the jackpot — only floor with LegendaryCrate, GimmickStone, pokemon_shiny, and Master Candy
  • Don't skip floors — each floor gives escalating tokens and keys. Full clear = 2,500 tokens
  • Trial Key chance — every floor has a 30% bonus Trial Key drop. Lucky runs = extra keys!
  • Save tokens — bigger items in the Token Shop need 500+ tokens. A full clear gives 2,500!

The Official Gym Challenge Rules

Battling Gyms in Pokefun is an exciting journey! You must prove your worth against NPCs before you can challenge the ultimate boss of the Gym: A REAL PLAYER!

Check Your NPC Wins

Want to know how many NPCs you've defeated to see if you meet the Gym requirements? Use the following command in-game:

/trainerprogress

Gym Progression Flow

1

Gain Required Total Wins

Before entering a Gym, you must prove yourself against regular trainers on the map (like F-Tier or E-Tier).

2

Defeat the Gym Entrance Trainers

Once you meet the Total Wins requirement, the Gym unlocks! Inside, you must defeat the 3 Entrance Trainers (NPCs).

3

Challenge the Sub Gym Leader (NPC)

After taking out all 3 Entrance Trainers, the Sub Gym Leader will accept your challenge.

Defeating this NPC is crucial. They will reward you with a special 1st Generation Pokemon Item which acts as your Official Gym Pass!

NPC Lv 100 | Player Max Lv 70
4

Battle the REAL Gym Leader (Player)

Take the Pass (Special Item) you just earned and give it to the REAL PLAYER Gym Leader!

Defeat them in a true PvP battle to earn your Gym Badge and top-tier rewards!

title: PokeFun Dungeons — Complete Player Guide
content:
PokeFun Dungeons — Complete Player Guide

Last updated: June 2026

Table of Contents

  1. What Are Dungeons?
  2. How to Join a Dungeon
  3. Alpha Pokemon Tiers
  4. Alpha Spawning & Behavior
  5. Quests
  6. Boss Battles
  7. Raids
  8. Loot Drops
  9. Rank Rewards
  10. Dungeon Shop
  11. Commands
  12. Cooldowns & Limits
  13. Tips & Strategy

1. What Are Dungeons?

Dungeons are instanced PvE battle arenas where you and your party fight waves of Alpha Pokemon (glowing, boosted wild Pokemon) and powerful Bosses. Each dungeon run has a time limit, quest objectives, and loot rewards. Complete quests, earn Dungeon Points, and climb the Rank system to unlock better rewards.

Available Dungeons (17)

  • Abyssal Depths
  • Ancient Ruins
  • Blazing Caldera
  • Crystal Caverns
  • Dragon's Lair
  • Frozen Tundra
  • Lunar Sanctum
  • Ocean Abyss
  • Shadow Realm
  • Sky Citadel
  • Solar Bastion
  • Storm Peak
  • Verdant Jungle
  • Void Gates

Each dungeon has different tier requirements, time limits, and quest objectives. Premium & fee-based dungeons may require an entry fee.

2. How to Join a Dungeon

  1. Form a party (minimum players varies per dungeon, typically 2–4).
  2. Use /warp dungeon or open the Dungeon Menu from the lobby to join a dungeon match.
  3. Once all party members are ready, the dungeon starts after a 10-second countdown.
  4. You'll be teleported to the dungeon world at the spawn point.
  5. You have a limited time (typically 20–50 minutes) to complete your quests.
  6. When the timer ends or all quests are complete, you'll be teleported to the reward area where you can catch reward Pokemon for 60 seconds.

3. Alpha Pokemon Tiers

Alphas are grouped into 7 standard tiers plus an Elite and Boss Tier. Higher tiers = stronger, bigger, and more rewarding alphas.

TierLevelDamage xHealth xSpeed xSizeIVsPointsGlow
Tier 130.5x1.0x0.5x0.501GRAY
Tier 251.0x2.0x0.7x0.753GREEN
Tier 3101.5x3.0x0.9x0.9105BLUE
Tier 4152.0x5.0x1.1x1.1158PURPLE
Tier 5203.0x8.0x1.2x1.22012RED
Tier 6304.0x10.0x1.3x1.32518DARK PURPLE
Tier 7355.0x14.0x1.4x1.53125GOLD
Boss Tier5010.0x15.0x1.8x2.03160DARK RED

Note: Some dungeons may also have an Elite tier (similar to Tier 6/7 range). Boss Tier alphas are legendary-only (Mewtwo, Rayquaza, Dialga, Arceus, etc.).

4. Alpha Spawning & Behavior

Initial Spawn

When a dungeon starts, 1 alpha per tier type spawns at its designated position — roughly 5–7 alphas in total. Not all positions are filled immediately.

Dynamic Respawn

Alphas respawn dynamically during the run:

  • Every 0.5 seconds, the dungeon checks for empty spawn positions.
  • Up to 2 new alphas spawn per check.
  • Killed alphas can respawn after just 10 seconds (200 ticks).
  • Maximum 15 alphas alive at any time (hard cap).

Aggression & Targeting

  • Alphas detect and target any player within the dungeon, regardless of distance.
  • They will only chase and attack if you are within 8 blocks (aggressiveRange).
  • Outside 8 blocks, they register you as a target but won't pursue — you can fight from a safe distance with ranged moves.
  • Alphas glow with their tier's particle effect (flame, dragon breath, soul fire).

Visual Effects by Tier

TierParticle TypeGlow Color

5. Quests

Each dungeon has 3–4 quests you must complete to earn rewards. Quest types:

  • KILL_ALPHA — Defeat a specific number of a given tier (e.g., "Defeat 15 BOSS_TIER alphas").
  • COLLECT_POINTS — Earn a target amount of Dungeon Points from killing alphas.
  • FIND_GEMS — Find a number of rare dungeon gems hidden in chests.

Quest progress is shared among party members. Once all quests are done, the dungeon run ends and rewards are distributed.

6. Boss Battles

Some dungeons have a dedicated boss room with powerful scripted boss Pokemon. Bosses have:

  • Level 100 with 31 IVs
  • 5x damage multiplier and 12x health multiplier
  • Size 3.0 — massive on the battlefield
  • Shiny by default with glowing effects
  • Special attacks: AOE, BEAM, or PROJECTILE every 6 seconds (120 ticks), dealing 50 damage with knockback
  • Special attacks have a 2-second warmup (40 ticks)

Weight determines how likely a boss is to be selected when the boss room activates.

7. Raids

Many dungeons have raid waves — periodic mass spawns of alphas that attack the party.

  • Raid waves occur every 2400 ticks (2 minutes) (if raid.json exists) or every 600 ticks (30 seconds) (fallback).
  • Each wave has multiple stages with different tiers, counts, and intervals.
  • Example raid waves (Abyssal Depths):
    • Wave 1: 6x Tier 2 alphas
    • Wave 2: 9x Tier 6 alphas
    • Wave 3: 4x Boss Tier alphas
    • Wave 4: 2x Shaymin (Boss Tier)
  • Raids spawn within 50 blocks of the dungeon spawn point.
  • Raid alphas count toward quest progress and can drop loot.

8. Loot Drops

9. Rank Rewards

After completing a dungeon run, you receive rank-based rewards. Your rank is determined by performance (kills, points, quest completion speed).

13. Tips & Strategy

Tip: Stay within 8 blocks to trigger alpha aggro. Alphas know where you are but will only chase within 8 blocks. Stay close to fight; kite from far for safety.
Tip: Focus on quest objectives first. Ignore unnecessary fights. Kill only the tier required by your quests to save time.
Tip: Use the 10-second respawn window. Killed alphas respawn after only 10 seconds. If you need many kills of one tier, stay near its spawn positions.
Tip: Watch out for raid waves. Every 2 minutes, a wave of alphas spawns. Be ready — raid alphas are tough and can overwhelm an unprepared party.
Tip: Save Dungeon Points for shiny keys. Shiny variant keys cost more but give shiny Pokemon. Save up!
Tip: Higher rank = better reward Pokemon. Rank 1 gives level 70 Pokemon. Kill more alphas and earn more points to boost your rank.
Tip: Bring strong Pokemon for Boss Tier alphas. Boss Tier alphas have 10x damage and 15x health. Don't face them with underleveled Pokemon.
Tip: Cooldown is per dungeon, per player. Each dungeon has a 24-hour individual cooldown. You can run different dungeons back-to-back.
🎁 New! Crate Keys in Rewards! Every rank has 40% chance to drop any of the 15 crate key types. Higher keys (LegendaryCrate, pokemon_shiny) are rarer. Grind more runs for better keys!
📊 Points Economy: ~200-250 points per dungeon run. Cheapest key (ItemCrate = 500pts) needs 2-3 runs. Best key (LegendaryCrateShiny = 8,400pts) needs ~34 runs. Play consistently!

PokeFusion Pokemon Fusion — Player Guide

Server-side only! You don't need to install any mod. Just join the server and use /fusion to open the fusion GUI!

What is PokeFusion?

PokeFusion lets you combine 2-3 Pokemon from your party into a brand new Pokemon using DNA Fusion Keys. The source Pokemon are consumed and you get a new fused Pokemon with best-of-both IVs!

Quick Facts

  • Max Pokemon per fusion: 3
  • Source consumed: Yes
  • Key required: DNA Fusion Key (1 per fusion)
  • IV mode: Best of Both
  • Broadcast: Fusions are announced in chat

How to Fuse — Step by Step

  1. Open GUI: Type /fusion or /pokefusion
  2. Select Pokemon: Click on party Pokemon in the bottom row (slots 36-41). Max 3 selections.
  3. Check Recipe: The GUI auto-detects if your selected species match a fusion recipe. The result preview slot shows what you'll get.
  4. Insert Keys: Make sure you have the required DNA Fusion Keys in your inventory. The GUI shows how many keys are needed.
  5. Click FUSE! Press the green FUSE button (slot 49). The keys and source Pokemon are consumed, and the result is added to your party.
Tip: If your party is full when fusing, the fusion is cancelled and your original Pokemon are restored. Make sure you have space!

Fusion GUI Layout

28, 31, 34Key requirement slots — shows which key type and how many needed

49FUSE button! Click to perform fusion

All Fusion Recipes

Below are all available fusions on the server. Each requires 1 DNA Fusion Key. Source Pokemon are consumed, result uses custom aspect (correct model), best-of-both IVs.

Fusion Key

All fusions require the DNA Fusion Key (Magma Cream). Keys are auto-detected in your inventory — no need to place in GUI.

Key Properties

  • Stack size: Always 1
  • Consumption: Keys are consumed on successful fusion
  • Acquisition: Buy from Dungeon Shop (200 DP) or Raid Shop (150 RP)

Where to Buy DNA Fusion Keys

DNA Fusion Keys (Magma Cream) are used in the /fusion GUI to fuse Pokemon. Available at:

Note: DNA Fusion Keys are different from Fusion Crate Keys. Crate Keys (/crate open FusionCrate) give pre-made fusion Pokemon from crates, while DNA Fusion Keys let you fuse your own Pokemon in the /fusion GUI.

FAQ

Q: Do I need to install anything to use fusion?

A: No! PokeFusion is completely server-side. You just need Cobblemon on your client.

Q: What happens to my original Pokemon?

A: By default, source Pokemon are consumed (removed). Make sure you want to fuse before clicking FUSE!

Q: How are IVs calculated?

A: All fusions use Best of Both — the highest IV from either parent for each stat.

Q: Can I get a shiny from fusion?

A: Yes! The fusion inherits the shiny status from the first selected Pokemon. The Garchomp recipe (Gabite + Salamence) always produces a shiny.

Q: Where do I get DNA Fusion Keys?

A: Buy them from the Dungeon Shop (200 Dungeon Points) or Raid Shop (150 Raid Points).

Q: What's the difference between DNA Fusion Key and Fusion Crate Key?

A: DNA Fusion Key (magma cream) is used in the /fusion GUI to fuse Pokemon. Fusion Crate Key is used with /crate open FusionCrate to get pre-made fusion Pokemon from crates.

Raid Pokemon Raids — Complete Player Guide

New to raids? Join at /warp raid and fight powerful boss Pokemon with other players! Earn Raid Points (RP), XP, BattlePoints, and rare rewards!

What are Raids?

Raids are cooperative PvE battles where players team up to defeat powerful boss Pokemon. Raids happen automatically on a schedule — listen for announcements or check /raid list to see active raids!

Why Raid?

  • Raid Points (RP) — Spend in the Raid Shop on rare items, keys, and gear
  • BattlePoints (BP) — Each boss defeated awards BP (1.25–15 BP depending on tier)
  • XP — Level up your raid rank for better rewards
  • Rare Pokemon — Catch the boss Pokemon after defeating it (if catch phase is enabled)
  • Items & Keys — Crate keys, healing items, EV items, and more

How to Join

  1. Warp to the raid area: /warp raid
  2. Check active raids: /raid list
  3. Join a raid: /raid join (joins the nearest active raid)
  4. Fight the boss with other players!

Commands

/raid listList all active raids
/raid joinJoin the nearest active raid

Raid Flow

  1. Announcement: A raid is announced in chat. Go to /warp raid and prepare!
  2. Setup Phase: Brief preparation period (bar turns blue). Get your Pokemon ready!
  3. Fight Phase: Battle the boss! The boss has high HP (scales with players) and powerful moves. Deal damage to earn rewards. Duration: ~10 minutes.
  4. Catch Phase (~60s): After the boss is defeated, you can throw Pokeballs to try and catch it! Use Premier or Ultra Balls for best chance.
  5. Rewards: Distributed based on damage dealt and participation.
No-Go Moves: The following moves/abilities/items are BANNED in raids and will NOT work: Destiny Bond, Ruination, Nature's Madness, Super Fang, OHKO moves (Fissure, Guillotine, Horn Drill, Sheer Cold), Perish Song, Wonder Guard ability, Healer ability, Quick Claw item.

Leaderboard

During a raid, you can see the top 5 damage dealers on the scoreboard (right side of screen). The top 3 earn bonus Raid Points!

Tips & Strategy

Bring your best Pokemon. Raid bosses have high stats (level 100-200+), scaled HP, and competitive movesets. Use super-effective moves and bring type advantages!
Deal damage for BP. Every 100 damage = 1 XP, and more damage = better rewards. Use setup moves (Swords Dance, Nasty Plot) early!
Team up! Raids are multiplayer — more players = faster kills. Coordinate with others for type coverage.
Catch the boss. During catch phase, use Premier or Ultra Balls for best catch rate. Shiny bosses are rare — don't miss your chance!
Use /raid shop frequently. Save up for legendary gear and shiny crate keys. The BP Voucher is the most efficient purchase for BattlePoints.
Reminder: Raids happen automatically! Listen for chat announcements and check /raid list. You can also see raid schedules in Discord.

Compete in ranked PvP battles, climb 15 tiers, and earn exclusive rewards including crate keys, Battle Points & Pokecoins!

  • BP amounts increase per tier: 5 BP → 500 BP per level
  • Pokecoins also added from Iron tier onwards!
  • Use BP in the Ranked Shop for exclusive items and keys
  • Higher tiers = way more BP & coins — climb to earn big!
